title: Exercise 1: Classes and Objects
lessonSummary: Great! You build a class and create objects with attributes.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: a class, an object, two attributes.
tasks.codeTemplate:
class Horse:
    pass

horse = Horse()
horse.name = "Blitz"
horse.level = 1
print(horse.name, horse.level)

tasks.instruction: Create a class Horse with `pass`. Create an object horse, set `name` to Blitz and `level` to 3 and print exactly Blitz has Level 3 with an f-string.
tasks.codeTemplate: # 🎯 Your solution here:

tasks.instruction: The empty class Horse is given. Create two objects horse (Blitz, level 1) and horse2 (Stella, level 1). Raise the level to 5 only for horse and print Blitz: 5 and Stella: 1 on two lines.

title: Exercise 2: The Constructor __init__
lessonSummary: Nice! Your constructor sets the starting values for every new object.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: a constructor with a default value.
tasks.codeTemplate:
class Horse:
    def __init__(self, name, level=1):
        self.name = name
        self.level = level

a = Horse("Blitz")
b = Horse("Stella", 5)
print(a.name, a.level)
print(b.name, b.level)

tasks.instruction: Write a class Horse with `__init__(self, name, level=1, energy=100)` that stores all three values. Create horse = Horse("Blitz", 4) and print exactly Blitz 4 100 with an f-string (name, level, energy).
tasks.codeTemplate: # 🎯 Your solution here:

tasks.instruction: The class Horse with `__init__(self, name, level=1)` is given. Create an object Sturm without a level and an object Stella with level 7 and print Sturm: Level 1 and Stella: Level 7 on two lines.

lessonSummary: Well done! Your objects can now do something.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: a method with self.
Write a class Horse with `__init__(self, name, level)` and the method `introduce(self)` that prints I am Blitz, Level 2. (name and level from `self`). Create Horse("Blitz", 2) and call the method.

tasks.instruction: The class Horse with the method `introduce()` is given. Create Horse("Stella", 4) and Horse("Sturm", 6) and call `introduce()` on both.

validation.expected:
I am Stella, Level 4.
I am Sturm, Level 6.

Write a class Horse with `__init__(self, name, energy)` and a method `is_tired(self)` that returns **True** if the energy is below 20 (otherwise False). Print the results for Horse("Blitz", 10) and Horse("Stella", 80) (two lines).

Write a class Horse with `__init__(self, name)` (attribute `wins` starts at 0) and the method `win(self)` that raises `wins` by 1. Call it three times and print exactly Wins: 3.

title: Exercise 6: Objects in Lists
lessonSummary: Nice! You manage whole groups of objects.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: looping over objects in a list.
The class Horse is given. Create the list `gruppe` with Horse("Blitz", 3), Horse("Stella", 8) and Horse("Sturm", 5) and print every name on its own line with a `for` loop.
The class Horse and the list `gruppe` (levels 3, 8, 5) are given. Find the object with the highest level with a loop and print exactly Strongest: Stella.
The class Horse and the list `gruppe` (levels 3, 8, 5) are given. Build the list `starke` of all names with level 5 or more with a list comprehension and print it with `print(starke)`.

title: Exercise 7: Passing Objects to Functions
lessonSummary: Well done! You now know how objects and functions work together.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: two names for one object.
tasks.codeTemplate:
class Horse:
    def __init__(self, name, level):
        self.name = name
        self.level = level

a = Horse("Blitz", 1)
b = a
b.level = 10
print(a.level)

tasks.instruction: The class Horse is given. Write a function `stronger(a, b)` that returns the object with the higher level. Compare Horse("Blitz", 4) and Horse("Stella", 9) and print exactly Winner: Stella.
The class Horse and the object `horse = Horse("Blitz")` are given. Give the object a second name `zweiter`, set the level to 9 through `zweiter` and print exactly Blitz: Level 9 through `horse`.

The class Horse and the list `gruppe` (levels 3, 8, 5) are given. Write a function `train_all(gruppe)` that does `level += 1` for everyone (no return). Call it and print exactly Sum: 19 (sum of all levels).

title: Extra Challenge 4: The Great Guild
lessonSummary: Done: classes work together with everything you have learned!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – functions and lists: the class Horse is given. Write `create_figure(name, level)` that returns an object. Create `gruppe` with create_figure("Blitz", 2) and create_figure("Stella", 5) and print exactly Group: 2 (length of the list).
Step 2 – randomness: the class Horse is given. Create horse = Horse("Blitz", random.randint(1, 5)) (`import random`) and print `1 <= horse.level <= 5` – the result must be True.

Step 3 – dictionary: the class Horse and the list `gruppe` (levels 3, 8, 5) are given. Build a dictionary `register` that maps every name to its object and print exactly Level: 8 for the entry Stella.

Step 4 – JSON: the class Horse is given. Create Horse("Blitz", 4), build the dictionary `daten` (`name`, `level`) from it and print `json.dumps(daten)`. Read the text back with `json.loads` and create a new object from it – finally print its name.
